beats.care: If you're travelling, compare regular and special buses before booking. A ₹200 regular fare can be ₹300 on a special.
beats.what: Harish Rao demanded TGSRTC roll back higher fares on festival special buses, citing a JBS to Karimnagar ticket rising from 230 to 400 rupees.
beats.why: Thousands are heading home for Bathukamma and Dasara. Reports say special buses charge up to 50 percent more than regular ones.

a.body: The government cut regular buses and charged high fares on 'specials' without adding buses. He says fares have risen five times in three years.
a.label: Harish Rao (BRS) says

b.body: Fares follow rules and a 2003 government order. It added 7,000 buses for the festive rush, and 97% of extra services since 10 October ran.
b.label: TGSRTC says

cards.body: Munsif Daily reported Uppal to Thorrur super-luxury going from about ₹300 to ₹430, and Mahabubnagar to MGBS from ₹220 to over ₹290. Crowds were heavy at MGBS, JBS, Uppal, KPHB, Dilsukhnagar and LB Nagar.
Under the state's Mahalakshmi scheme, women travel free on many TGSRTC buses. Harish Rao questioned charging men more while women ride free; TGSRTC says the scheme runs smoothly.
cards.title: why do women ride free?

opts: Special services may charge extra under rules
cards.q: Why do festival special buses cost more?
cards.why: TGSRTC says special services are priced under a 2003 order that allows higher fares during the rush.

hook: Going home for Dasara? Why your bus ticket may cost *up to 50% more*

learn.t: TGSRTC says festival special-bus fares are set under a 2003 government order, which lets special services charge more than regular ones.

event.label: Harish Rao vs TGSRTC on fares
